== Biography ==
{{Ireland Native}}
Sarah was the daughter of [[Glasgow-1701|James Glasgow]]
<ref>There were several James Glasgows; this particular one is matched by his daughter [[Glasgow-1707|Nancy]] listing Silas W Henry as brother-in-law in her will.</ref>
She was born about 1848.<ref>Age 78 at death Feb 1927.</ref>
She lived at Killycurragh as of 1870.

On 19 Mar 1870 at 3rd Cookstown Presbyterian, she married Silas Weir Henry of Killycurragh, son of James Henry jnr., farmer. Witnessed by Samuel Johnston Glasgow and William Weir Whan.
<ref>[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/0368da2722990 Silias Henry, Sarah Glasgow, 1870, Cookstown] at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages</ref>

She passed away 12 Feb 1927, age 78, widow, at the residence of her son in Ballygrainey, Greyabbey, County Down. Her health had been failing for some time and she was attended by her daughter and daughter-in-law. She was interred at the New Cemetery, Cookstown, plot OP/A/834.
<ref>D/1927/199/1024/15/494	Sarah	Henry	12th February 1927	78		Female	Newtownards</ref>
The chief mourners were:
<ref>[https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0002006/19270226/139/0008 "Obituary - Mrs S W Henry"], ''Mid-Ulster Mail'' - Saturday 26 February 1927</ref>
* Wm James Henry, Alex Bismarck Henry, Stuart Knox Henry, and Ernest H Henry (sons)
* Herbert N McAdoo, Ernest Couldrey, Samuel J Stewart and Robert Agnew (sons-in-law)
* [[Glasgow-1726|John Glasgow]] (brother)
* [[Henry-8395|Isaac H Henry]] (brother-in-law)
* Victor, Jim Herbert and Max Henry, John Agnew and Robert Samuel Stewart (grandsons)
* Wm James, Fred C, Robert J, Harold, Thomas J, Alan and Tom Glasgow; Thomas Warnock, Hugh J Nesbitt, George Black, Wm Weir, James Weir, Henry C Bell, John Tomb, Knox Henry, Wm Henry, James M Henry (nephews)
A marriage for Sarah Glasgow and Henry was registered on 19 March 1870 in the Cookstown district.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 19 March 1870, Cookstown district, M/1870/L1/1131/2/44.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1701]] is assessed at 98% (proved). Sarah's 1870 marriage names father James and Killycurragh, while Nancy's will specifically calls Silas W Henry brother-in-law. That cross-reference identifies James junior's daughter rather than merely a same-named bride.

Selected Glasgow-1701 fatherhood of Glasgow-745; maternal identity and upstream ancestry are separate.

Next useful test: Compare original marriage and Nancy's will.

Source basis already held: [https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/0368da2722990 Silias Henry, Sarah Glasgow, 1870, Cookstown (https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/0368 da2722990) at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
